body.translated_text: Now, [the work] called <s>Yuktiṣaṣṭikārikā</s> (Sixty Verses on Reasoning). Homage to <s>Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta</s> (the youthful one).

children.translated_text: Homage to that lord of sages, the teacher of dependent [origination],
by whose this method, arising and passing away have been denied.
Those whose mind has transcended existence and non-existence, resting on nothing —
by them is the profound, unsupported meaning of conditions understood. || 1 ||
First, non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>), which produces all faults, has been refuted;

children.text: nirvartyate yathā yuktayā bhāvo 'pi śrvavaṇaṃ kuru || Yukti_2
children.translated_text: as existence too is refuted by reasoning — listen! || 2 ||
If existence were truly real as conceived by the childish,

children.text: vimokṣastadabhāvena ko necchet kim na kārnāt || Yukti_3
children.translated_text: then liberation would be [achieved] through its non-existence — who would not desire it? For what reason [not]? || 3 ||

children.text: vimokṣo nāsti bhāvena bhāvo nāsti hyabhāvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Liberation does not exist as a [real] entity; an entity does not exist from non-existence;
through the thorough knowledge of both existence and non-existence, even the great one is liberated. || 4 ||

children.text: nirvāṇam caiva lokaṃ ca manyante tattvadarśinaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and also the world — the seers of reality consider [them as non-different];

children.text: naiva lokaṃ na nirvānaṃ manyante tattvadarśinaḥ || Yukti_5
children.translated_text: neither the world nor <s>nirvāṇa</s> — the seers of reality consider [either as ultimately real]. || 5 ||

children.text: nirvānaṃ ca bhavaścaiva dvayameva na vidyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and existence — this duality simply does not exist;
the thorough knowledge (<s>parijñāna</s>) of existence itself is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>. || 6 ||
Just as cessation is imagined for a thing that arises and ceases,
this cessation is [itself] illusory (<s>māyākṛta</s>) — so it is accepted by the wise. || 7 ||

children.text: samskṛto na parijñāto nirodho vibhave sati |
children.translated_text: The conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) is not thoroughly known; cessation [is posited] when there is destruction;

children.text: pratyakṣam bhūyate kasmin vibhavo jñāyate katham || Yukti_8
children.translated_text: in what does perception arise? How is destruction known? || 8 ||
If by the cessation of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) there were not the destruction of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>),

children.text: yadā cāyaṃ niruddhaḥ syāttadā mokṣo bhavisyati || Yukti_9
children.translated_text: when this [aggregate] were to cease, then liberation would arise. || 9 ||
For one who sees with right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) what has arisen from the condition of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>),
neither arising nor cessation is found to be logically [tenable]. || 10 ||

children.text: evam paśyati dharmaḥ yo nirvānam vā katam tathā |
children.translated_text: He who thus sees <s>dharma</s>, or <s>nirvāṇa</s> in that way —

children.text: dharmajñānam paraṃ yatra bhedastu tatra vidyate || Yukti_11
children.translated_text: where there is supreme <s>dharma</s>-knowledge, there too differentiation exists. || 11 ||
He who conceives the birth of an extremely subtle thing
and does not see the object as arisen from conditions — he is unwise. || 12 ||
If monks (<s>bhikṣu</s>) whose defilements (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) are destroyed are turned away from <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: kutaḥ sampannabuddhaiśca tasyārambho na bhāṣitaḥ || Yukti_13
children.translated_text: why have the fully awakened <s>Buddhas</s> not spoken of its beginning? || 13 ||
If there were a beginning, there would be an extreme grasping of views (<s>dṛṣṭiparigraha</s>);

children.text: yaḥ pratītyasamutpādastasya purvaṃ paraṃ vā kim || Yukti_14
children.translated_text: of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), what is before or after? || 14 ||
How is what has already arisen first prevented afterwards?
Liberation, devoid of beginning and end, is renowned as illusion-like (<s>māyopama</s>). || 15 ||

children.text: bhavatīdam yadā māyā namkṣyatīti tadaiva hi |
children.translated_text: 'This exists,' 'this is <s>māyā</s>,' 'it will perish' — [thinking] thus indeed,
one overcome by the knowledge of illusion is deluded by the knowledge of illusion. || 16 ||

children.text: yathā marīcikā māyā bhavam buddhayā hi paśyati |
children.translated_text: He who sees existence with wisdom as a mirage (<s>marīcikā</s>) or illusion (<s>māyā</s>)

children.text: purvāntam vāparāntam vā na dṛṣṭayā parikliśyate || Yukti_17
children.translated_text: is not afflicted by the view of either a prior or a posterior end. || 17 ||
Those who conceive the conditioned as involving the notions of destruction and arising

children.text: pratītyotpādacakreṇa vijānanti na te jagat || Yukti_18
children.translated_text: do not understand the world through the wheel of dependent origination (<s>pratītyotpādacakra</s>). || 18 ||
What has arisen depending on that [condition] is indeed not arisen by itself;

children.text: svayam yadā yadutpannamutpannam nāma tat katham || Yukti_19
children.translated_text: when something arises by itself — how can that be called 'arisen'? || 19 ||
[What is] pacified through the destruction of causes alone is understood as 'destroyed';

children.text: svabhāvena hi yatkṣīṇam tat kṣīṇamucyate katham || Yukti_20
children.translated_text: but what is destroyed by its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — how can that be called 'destroyed'? || 20 ||

children.text: na kaścidanutpannam nirodho 'pi na vai tathā |
children.translated_text: No one is [truly] unborn; cessation too is not like that.
The intended meaning has been shown through the function of arising and destruction. || 21 ||
From the knowledge of arising, [comes the knowledge of] destruction; from the knowledge of destruction, impermanence (<s>anityatā</s>);
and from the understanding of impermanence, the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>) is indeed realized. || 22 ||
He who thoroughly knows dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), free from arising and destruction —
by him alone is the ocean of existence (<s>bhavābdhi</s>) crossed. || 23 ||
Ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), whose self-conceptions are perverted by [notions of] the existent and non-existent,
beings caught in the lineage of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), deceived by the thought of self (<s>ātman</s>). || 24 ||
By the wise, things are contemplated as empty (<s>śūnya</s>), impermanent (<s>anitya</s>), and without self (<s>anātmaka</s>);
and the accumulation of deceptive <s>dharmas</s> is seen as isolated [from any self]. || 25 ||
Having no root, there is no permanence — [it is] unsupported, without foundation;
arisen from the cause of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), devoid of beginning, middle, and end. || 26 ||
like a ship in a city of delusion — he who sees the world as like an illusion (<s>māyā</s>). || 27 ||
In this, the world from <s>Brahmā</s> downward appears as if real;

children.text: satyanmṛṣetyuktamāryena tatra kā śiṣyate parā || Yukti_28
children.translated_text: 'Real and false' was said by the Noble One — what higher [truth] remains beyond that? || 28 ||
This world, blinded by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), is driven by the current of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>);
how can the vision of merit for one who is wise and free from craving be the same [as theirs]? // <s>Yukti</s> 29 //
In the beginning, having seen this reality, [the Buddha] teaches that 'everything exists';
knowing the meaning, yet unattached, one is later surely discriminated [from the ignorant]. // <s>Yukti</s> 30 //
Those who do not know the discriminated meaning proceed on mere hearing alone;
those whose merit is unbroken [attain realization] — the rest of the people are cut off. // <s>Yukti</s> 31 //
Actions are connected with fruits — this world has been properly taught;
but the thorough knowledge of its true nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) has been taught as 'unborn' (<s>anutpanna</s>). // <s>Yukti</s> 32 //
'I' and 'mine' are spoken by people according to necessity of function;
likewise, the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and <s>dhātus</s> (elements) are taught according to functional necessity. // <s>Yukti</s> 33 //
The great elements and the rest are proclaimed, and likewise the collection in consciousness;

children.text: tajjñānena viyukttena mṛṣaiva na vikalpitam || Yukti_34
children.translated_text: separated from the knowledge of that [reality], it is simply false — not [merely] conceptually constructed. // <s>Yukti</s> 34 //
<s>Nirvāṇa</s> alone is the one truth — thus the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) have declared;

children.text: nāva śiṣṭam tadā satyamevam vijñena kalpitam || Yukti_35
children.translated_text: the remainder then is not truth — this is what the wise one has determined. // <s>Yukti</s> 35 //
As long as there is distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>) of the mind, so long is it the domain of <s>Māra</s>;

children.text: evambhūto bhavedyatra nā doṣo jāyate kathaṃ || Yukti_36
children.translated_text: in such a state, how can faults not arise? // <s>Yukti</s> 36 //
Since the world has been proclaimed by the <s>Buddhas</s> as having ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) as its condition,
therefore, that this world is conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) — why does this not stand to reason? // <s>Yukti</s> 37 //
When ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is ceased, cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) arises, just as

children.text: ajñānato hi samkalpa iti kim na vidhīyate || Yukti_38
children.translated_text: conceptual construction (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) arises from ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) — why is this not established? // <s>Yukti</s> 38 //

children.text: hetutaḥ sambhavo yasya sthiti rna pratyayairvinā |
children.translated_text: That whose arising is from causes, whose persistence is not without conditions,
whose cessation is from the absence of conditions — how is that understood as 'existing'? // <s>Yukti</s> 39 //
If those who assert [inherent] existence hold that persistence depends on a supreme entity,

children.text: tadaiva hi sthitā mārge na kaściditasmayastataḥ || Yukti_40
children.translated_text: then indeed they would be standing on the [correct] path — but no one goes astray from that. // <s>Yukti</s> 40 //
All those who rely on the <s>Buddha</s>'s path assert 'impermanent';

children.text: kena vādena gṛhyante bhāvāḥ santi parā iti || Yukti_41
children.translated_text: by what argument are they grasped [in the error that] entities exist as supreme? // <s>Yukti</s> 41 //
Where the deliberation 'this is or is not' is not found,

children.text: idam satyamado veti paṇḍitaiḥ kathamucyatai || Yukti_42
children.translated_text: 'this is true, that is not' — how can this be said by the wise? // <s>Yukti</s> 42 //
Without appropriating, they too neither desire the world nor the self;
the arising of [views about] permanence, impermanence, and the rest is removed through abandoning false views. // <s>Yukti</s> 43 //
For those who have appropriated entities as real, their truths have been established;

children.text: tatra liṅgādayo doṣāḥ prajāyante na vā kathaṃ || Yukti_44
children.translated_text: therein, faults such as the [existence of] marks (<s>liṅga</s>) and the rest — do they arise or not, and how? // <s>Yukti</s> 44 //

children.text: yān hi dharmānupādāya dṛṣṭaścandro jale yathā |
children.translated_text: Having appropriated which <s>dharmas</s>, [one perceives] like the moon seen in water —

children.text: tatra satyam mṛṣā naiva kāmaṃ dṛṣṭyā na hāritaḥ || Yukti_45
children.translated_text: therein is neither truly true nor false; indeed, [the wise one] is not abandoned by [right] vision. // <s>Yukti</s> 45 //
Arising from attachment and aversion, the embrace of fierce, corrupted views,
and disputes arising from them — [all these occur] when [inherent] existence is accepted. // <s>Yukti</s> 46 //

children.text: sa hetuḥ sarvadṛṣṭīnām kleśotpatti rna tam vinā |
children.translated_text: That [acceptance] is the cause of all views; the arising of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) does not occur without it;
therefore, when that is thoroughly understood (<s>parijñāta</s>), views and afflictions are completely destroyed. // <s>Yukti</s> 47 //
And by what is it thoroughly understood? Through seeing dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>);
'What arises dependently is unborn' — thus spoke the best of those who know reality. // <s>Yukti</s> 48 //
One who, having overcome false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>), holds the unreal as real,
the grasping of [false] reasoning and the rest is considered [the sequence of] attachment and action, in order. // <s>Yukti</s> 49 //

children.text: mahātmanām na pakṣo vā vitarko vā na vidyate |
children.translated_text: For the great ones, there is no thesis nor reasoning;

children.text: yeṣām na vidyate pakṣeḥ parapakṣaḥ kutasteṣām || Yukti_50
children.translated_text: for those who have no thesis, how can there be an opposing thesis? // <s>Yukti</s> 50 //
In whomever [the mind] takes shelter, one is bitten by the poison-snakes of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);

children.text: calaṃ vāniṣṭhitam cittaṃ na tiṣṭhatyanāśritam || Yukti_51
children.translated_text: the mind that is restless and unsteady does not abide without a support. // <s>Yukti</s> 51 //

children.text: sāśraya cittavāna sattveḥ kleśodbhūto viṣo mahān |
children.translated_text: A being with a mind that has support — the great poison of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) arises [in him];

children.text: sadā pṛthagajano hīnaḥ kleśasarpena gṛhītaḥ || Yukti_52
children.translated_text: always, the ordinary person of inferior [understanding] is seized by the serpent of afflictions. // <s>Yukti</s> 52 //

children.text: prativimbe yathā rāgo loke ca mohavandhanāt |
children.translated_text: Just as there is attachment to a reflection in the world, through the bond of delusion,

children.text: viṣayapinjaro sakto bālo hi satyasamjñayā || Yukti_53
children.translated_text: the childish one, trapped in the cage of sense-objects, is attached [to them] through the notion of [their] reality. // <s>Yukti</s> 53 //
Through the eyes, one indeed perceives objects by means of image-cognition;
unattached to the mud of <s>karma</s> — such is the nature of the great ones. // <s>Yukti</s> 54 //
People attached to form are deluded; the middling ones are free from attachment;

children.text: rūpasvabhāvavijño yo vimukto buddhimān paraḥ || Yukti_55
children.translated_text: one who knows the true nature of form — the supreme one, the wise, is liberated. // <s>Yukti</s> 55 //
Having turned away from the contemplation of pleasure, free from the abandonment of passion,
seeing [all things] as a magical person (<s>māyāpuruṣa</s>), one will be ceased [from saṃsāra]. // <s>Yukti</s> 56 //
One who is tormented by false knowledge, partaking of the fault of the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>),
through conceptually constructing existence and non-existence — knowledge of [true] meaning does not arise. // <s>Yukti</s> 57 //
Without support, those free from passion indeed become free from attachment;

children.text: arāge rāgavardhāste na sāśrayā mahātmanaḥ || Yukti_58
children.translated_text: for the great ones (<s>mahātmā</s>), those [defilements] that increase attachment are not supported, being free from attachment. (verse 58)
Those whose minds are isolated (<s>viviktacetas</s>), whose consciousness is restless and flickering —
even bitten by the serpent of defilements (<s>kleśasarpa</s>), they have crossed the ocean of existence (<s>bhavāmbūdhi</s>), uninjured. (verse 59)

children.text: śāstreṇānena janānām punyam jñānam ca sancitam |
children.translated_text: By this treatise, merit (<s>puṇya</s>) and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) have been accumulated for beings;
through the arising of the activity of merit and knowledge, may both [self and others] attain the supreme reality. (verse 60)

body.translated_text: Essenceless like a plantain trunk, like a <s>gandharva</s>-city,
Thus the <s>Yuktiṣaṣṭikākārikā</s> (Sixty Verses on Reasoning) is complete.
From the mouth of the noble <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, this treatise,

children.translated_text: heard by the Indian <s>paṇḍita</s> <s>Muditaśrī</s>,
was written in the Tibetan language by the Tibetan <s>paṇḍita</s> named <s>Sūryakīrti</s>
from the <s>Pātchava</s> region, residing in Tibet.
